collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE III: DEFENSE, RAIDS AND THE FALLEN (LCC-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
"If anyone comes to raid our homeland, we'll be ready." Isola's people are peaceful but no pushovers: stamping dances and war chants, watch fires and plans, raids fended off or not, prisoners and bargains, and how the village honors those who defended it.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Among the raiders who fled was a teenager who stayed behind, frightened: take them in, or return them to their family.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The raiders fled and left behind a frightened teenager hiding in the mangroves, who says (other.he/she) was made to come and never wanted to. (other.He/she) has asked to stay on Isola. (subject) wants to take (other.him/her) in. (friend) says (other.his/her) family will be looking for (other.him/her) and (other.he/she) belongs with them. What should the village do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) takes the teen into (subject.his/her) own family. The teen is silent and watchful for a long time. Then one evening (other.he/she) laughs at something (subject) says, and keeps laughing. The village sends word to the teen's family that (other.he/she) is safe, and may visit whenever (other.he/she) likes.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) takes the teen home under a white cloth. (other.His/her) family weeps to see (other.him/her). The teen looks back at Isola from the beach. Whether (other.he/she) will ever come back, nobody knows. (friend) leaves (other.him/her) a carved fish, so (other.he/she) remembers the way.
